subject: Capacity fracture: containment closure, follow-up evidence request
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@quantaflow.ai>
To: irene_choi@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: sudden latency/error spikes - QuantaFlow production impact

Hi Irene / Marissa,

We saw a sharp spike in generation latency and 5xx errors starting around 08:50 PT this morning for our Reserved GPU cluster (region: us-west). Latency rose from our steady 120ms p95 to >3s and a subset of requests started returning 502/504 intermittently. This impacted our real-time ranking pipeline and caused downstream timeouts.

We kicked fallback to the hosted small model but that caused quality regressions. Can you confirm whether this was an infrastructure issue on Redwood's side or something in our rollout? We need:
- immediate status on root cause and containment
- logs for the period 08:45-09:30 (allocation/eviction/autoscaler traces)
- ETA for a full timeline and post-incident wrap-up so we can prep an external postmortem on our side

Attached are a couple of screenshots and a short list of example request IDs. Happy to jump on a call.

Thanks,
Daniel Park
Head of Platform Reliability
QuantaFlow
Attachments: qflow-screens-03-18.png, qflow-reqids-03-18.txt
From: irene_choi@redwood.ai
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@quantaflow.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: sudden latency/error spikes - QuantaFlow production impact

Daniel — thank you for the heads up and the request IDs.

Short update: our on-call observed a saturation event in the reserved GPU pool that matches the timeframe you reported. We have activated the emergency fallback ladder for your tenant (traffic was routed to the warmed hosted variant for ~18 minutes starting at 08:58 PT) and the autoscaler was temporarily constrained during the spike.

Immediate next steps we have taken:
- Scoped impact and moved a portion of traffic to the warmed hosted fallback to restore throughput.
- Captured allocator and autoscaler traces (we're attaching a first-pass trace set).
- Opened an internal RCA ticket and pulled in runtime (Ben) to investigate kernel-level allocation behavior.

We do not have a final root cause yet. Can you confirm whether you ran any heavy model rollouts or increased concurrency from your side between 08:30-09:10? If not, we'll continue triage and deliver the logs you asked for in the next 3 hours.

I'll schedule a short call at 10:15 PT to sync if that works for you — otherwise reply with preferred time.

— Irene Choi
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: irene_choi@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, Daniel Park <daniel.park@quantaflow.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: sudden latency/error spikes - QuantaFlow production impact

On Wed, Mar 18, 2026 at 09:28 AM Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Daniel — thank you for the heads up and the request IDs.

Quick technical summary from runtime team (triage notes):
- Root cause (preliminary): a combination of autoscaler race during rapid allocation + an allocator backpressure regression introduced in the 2026.2.1 runtime patch. The autoscaler attempted to spin up nodes but a tight loop in allocation backoff caused a subset of allocation requests to timeout and evict warm workers, which led to transient coldstarts and queued requests.
- Observable signals: spike in eviction rates at 08:52, queued depth increase at 08:53, and short-lived warm cache misses driving increased token latency.

Mitigations performed:
1) Immediate: forced activation of the warmed hosted fallback for your tenant to relieve the reserved pool (completed 08:58 — 09:16 PT).
2) Short-term fix: rolled back the allocator backoff change on the affected cell at 09:10 PT (this restored normal allocation behavior).
3) Ongoing: a hotfix build to address the autoscaler race is being prepared; ETA for canary is 48 hours.

Attachments included in this thread: autoscaler-alloc-trace.txt (allocator traces), pool-telemetry-03-18.csv (telemetry snapshot), redwood-quick-rollback-notes.pdf (rollback actions taken).

Data we need from QuantaFlow to complete RCA:
- Any high-concurrency experiment or spike in request concurrency between 08:30-09:00 PT.
- Example request payloads for samples that returned 502/504 if available.

We'll provide a full timeline and a draft postmortem by EOD; if you need the logs sooner we'll push them to the Drive link and share access.

— Ben Carter
Principal Runtime Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: irene_choi@redwood.ai
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@quantaflow.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: sudden latency/error spikes - QuantaFlow production impact

Hi Daniel — final update for today and next actions.

Summary (closed containment):
- Cause: autoscaler allocation race + allocator backoff regression (introduced in runtime patch 2026.2.1). The combination resulted in brief eviction and coldstart amplification across the reserved pool.
- Impact window: 2026-03-18T08:50:00-2026-03-18T09:16:00 PT (requests with IDs you provided map to that interval).
- Customer-visible symptoms: p95 latency increased, intermittent 502/504s. No data loss.

What we did:
- Immediate fallback to warmed hosted variant for your tenant, reducing errors while preserving throughput.
- Rolled back the allocator backoff on affected cells to restore allocation behavior.
- Collected traces and telemetry; attached a curated set for your team.

What we'll do next (commitments):
- Draft postmortem (internal + redacted customer summary) by EOD 2026-03-18 (link: https://drive.redwood.com/file/d/1a2b3c-postmortem-draft).
- Hotfix for autoscaler race canary within 48 hours; full rollout after validation.
- We'll propose a tenant-specific mitigation (reserved warm cushion) and offer a credit for the incident window; formal credit proposal included in the postmortem.

Requested from QuantaFlow:
- Confirm whether you executed any internal concurrency spike or rollout (reply with a short yes/no and any approximate timestamps).
- If possible, send a couple of representative payloads that failed so our runtime team can repro the error modes.

Attachments included: autoscaler-alloc-trace.txt, pool-telemetry-03-18.csv, redwood-quick-rollback-notes.pdf. We also added those files to the Drive link above and to your HubSpot deal record (link: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234569/deal/QF-DF-8421).

If you'd like a short review call tomorrow to go through the draft postmortem before it's finalized, we can do 09:30 PT.

Appreciate the quick collaboration — we'll keep this channel open for evidence exchange.

Best,
Irene Choi
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
